results.title: 智能奈米機器人物質與可變形自主車體極限 1/90 Intelligent Nanorobotic Matter and Morphing Autonomous Vehicle Bodies at the Limit STARLI | YULI NANO SUPERCAR TRILOGY | PART I Research Institute XXXVI / Flagship 01 of 90 Author: Feng Cheng-en (33) x STARLI / 星璃 Research Working Edition v1.0 | 31 October 2026 | 777 pages This 777-page English research working monograph proposes a falsifiable, scaled engineering architecture for programmable robotic matter and morphing autonomous vehicle structures. It asks whether identified modules can form a load-bearing body panel, pass between two registered geometries and retain verified structural integrity under hidden connector defects. The work is strictly hypothesis-forming, non-occupancy and not an automotive safety or roadworthiness claim. Its three-way research coupling joins programmable matter, distributed robotics and vehicle load paths. The fundamental scientific test separates exterior shape change from graph rigidity, measured weak-direction stiffness, connector preload, joint slip, reversible structural control and an independently traceable load transfer path. A minimum 1:10 modular panel competes against matched-mass fixed monocoque and passive modular lattice baselines under pre-registered blinded disturbances. Aborted trials, rejected units, repair events, energy overhead and uncertainty remain in the complete experimental denominator. Thirty distinct mathematical research plates cover graph-rigidity rank, constrained stiffness assembly, weak-mode stability, structural load margin, Euler buckling, friction cones, shear transfer, connector hysteresis, fatigue, crack propagation, geometry error, rigid registration, kinematic Jacobians, actuator work, electrical dissipation, thermal balance, safe control, correlated metrology, emergency stop latency, material mass closure, redundancy, reproducibility and conjunctive release. Each plate distinguishes physical construction, measurable units, assumptions, blind falsification and chapter interfaces. Eighty-two chapters are paired with 410 individually paginated investigations. The monograph additionally proposes 200 Research Gates and 33 genuinely different Phoenix Answer Embryos, including rigidity witnesses, connector passports, metrology transfer kits, half-transition recovery tests, sensor-refusal protocols and successor-ready research seeds. These items are research invitations and candidate evidence objects; they are not completed experimental outcomes. DOI evidence ancestry and component research sources: - 10.5281/zenodo.23318840 - Flagship 13 mother monograph, DOI supplied by author (metadata not independently confirmed here). - 10.5281/zenodo.23318839 - Flagship 13 all-version ancestry, DOI supplied by author (metadata not independently confirmed here). - 10.1038/s41467-024-53123-6 - Robo-Matter towards reconfigurable multifunctional smart materials (2024). - 10.1038/s41467-025-60982-0 - Modular shape-changing tensegrity-blocks enable self-assembling robotic structures (2025). - 10.1145/3653671 - From Conventional to Programmable Matter Systems (2024 review). - 10.1007/s10846-024-02067-6 - Reconfiguration strategies for modular robots (2024 review). - 10.1177/02783649241283847 - Modular robot mechanisms and design (2025 survey). - 10.1126/scirobotics.adz1999 - Modular reconfigurable robots and application needs (2026 review). The cited studies and reviews support component mechanisms and known challenges. They do not provide evidence that the integrated morphing vehicle concept has been built, road-tested or approved. The candidate's core release policy is conjunctive: load-path continuity, bounded geometry error, valid independent metrology, physical stop authority and reproducible external replay must pass together. This monograph carries the series imprint 1/90, preserving the first book's position within the ninety-volume STARLI YULI Nano Supercar Trilogy. The subsequent research lineage extends to modular assembly, autonomous mobile habitats and self-expanding cities while retaining explicit experimental and human-governance boundaries. results.title: Adaptive Control of Robot Manipulators With Uncertain Kinematics and Dynamics
results.snippet: In this paper, we investigate the adaptive control problem for robot manipulators with both the uncertain kinematics and dynamics. We propose two adaptive control schemes to realize the objective of task-space trajectory tracking irrespective of the uncertain kinematics and dynamics. The proposed controllers have the desirable separation property, and we also show that the first adaptive controller with appropriate modifications can yield improved performance, without the expense of conservative gain choice. The performance of the proposed controllers is shown by numerical simulations.

results.title: Analysis and design of model predictive control frameworks for dynamic operation -- An overview
results.snippet: This article provides an overview of model predictive control (MPC) frameworks for dynamic operation of nonlinear constrained systems. Dynamic operation is often an integral part of the control objective, ranging from tracking of reference signals to the general economic operation of a plant under online changing time-varying operating conditions. We focus on the particular challenges that arise when dealing with such more general control goals and present methods that have emerged in the literature to address these issues. The goal of this article is to present an overview of the state-of-th…

results.title: Passive iFIR Filters for Data-Driven Control
results.snippet: We consider the design of a new class of passive iFIR controllers given by the parallel action of an integrator and a finite impulse response filter. iFIRs are more expressive than PID controllers but retain their features and simplicity. The paper provides a model-free data-driven design for passive iFIR controllers based on virtual reference feedback tuning. Passivity is enforced through constrained optimization (three different formulations are discussed). The proposed design does not rely on large datasets or accurate plant models.

# 机器人运动学、控制与 ROS 2 生态：近 1-2 年前沿增量快照（七维追踪）

**日期**：2026-11-25（UTC）  
**领域**：机器人运动学、控制算法、ROS 2 生态、具身智能基础设施  
**检索源数量**：30 条可引用证据源（编号 [1]–[2]）  
**方法论**：frontier-tracking / deep-research / evidence-grading / frontier-watch  

---

## 1. 进展与热点（Progress & Hotspots）

> **一句话增量判断**：近 1-2 年运动学与控制算法呈现“经典自适应控制回顾巩固 + MPC 动态运行框架系统化梳理 + 数据驱动被动控制新范式 + VLA 基础模型落地桌面操作”四大并行热点；ROS 2 生态核心痛点聚焦于 sim-to-real 标准化基准缺失；政策层面 ISO 10218/ISO/TS 15066 2025 版修订落地，安全标准与协作机器人合规要求同步收紧。

### 2.2 ROS 2 工程落地现状

- **仿真-真机评估工具链碎片化**：现有仿真基准（Isaac Sim、MuJoCo、Gazebo 等）推动了研究，但通用策略的真实世界评估滞后，缺乏系统性的 sim-to-real 迁移基准设计原则 [7]。
- **真机竞赛基准较早**：Real Robot Challenge (2021) 为三指灵巧手提供真机操作基准，但时间较早，当前关注度有限，需结合 Open X-Embodiment、DROID 等最新数据集综合考察 [8]。
- **> 待核实**：ROS 2 Humble/Iron/Jazzy 版本在工业级实时控制、安全认证、OPC UA/TSN 集成方面的最新产品化落地案例。

## 4. 瓶颈与拐点（Bottleneck & Inflection）

> **一句话增量判断**：四大瓶颈正逼近拐点：(1) 仿真-真机评估标准化缺口 → RSS 2025 工作坊提出三大设计原则，社区共识形成中；(2) MPC 高频伺服层计算延迟 → 专用求解器与硬件加速 (FPGA/GPU) 使 1kHz+ MPC 成为可能；(3) VLA 基座模型数据飞轮 → MR0 等大厂模型展示 1.5 万小时轨迹规模，数据获取成本成为新瓶颈；(4) 协作机器人安全标准修订 → ISO 10218-1/2:2025 与 ISO/TS 15066 融合落地，合规成本与创新速度博弈加剧。
